title: bbox_note_resolve has no batch mode and rewrites the entire note store on every single-id call
wanted_capability:
A batch bbox_note_resolve (resolve N note ids in one call: one lock acquisition, one mutation pass, one persist) AND a fix for the per-call cost. Today resolving M notes requires M separate MCP calls, and each one is slow because NoteStore::save (src/notes.rs:221) calls json_store::atomic_write_json_locked — a full serialize of the ENTIRE note store to a temp file + fsync + rename, under a cross-process file lock. So resolving 40 notes = 40 full-store rewrites serialized on the lock. Same blocking-fs-on-write-under-lock pattern the threads already fixed for the task store via the single-writer TaskPersister actor.</wanted_capability>
<parameter name="missing_primitive">A batch-resolve param on bbox_note_resolve (ids: [..]) that mutates once and saves once; and/or moving the note-store persist to the coalesced single-writer actor pattern (like TaskPersister) so per-note writes don't each rewrite the whole file under the lock.
fallback_used: Resolved 40 driver notes via 40 sequential single-id bbox_note_resolve calls; operator observed each is slow (full-store atomic rewrite per call).
notes: Operator-directed: "bbox_note_resolve is still slow ... probably needs a batch mode + root causing." Root cause = full-store atomic_write_json_locked per resolve. Surfaced while cleaning up a 40-note storm (see the nudge-compulsion gap).
resolution_note: Implemented bbox_note_resolve batch resolution. The tool now accepts ids=[...] with a shared note and notes={id: detail} for per-note resolution details; all target IDs are validated before mutation and the existing StorePersister durable path performs one persist ack for the batch.
